title_en: Yi Lijun v. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Panjin Branch — dispute over bank card
ruling_gist_en: As a professional institution handling financial business, a bank holds an evident and dominant advantage when handling savings and other businesses for natural persons, while natural persons are in a relatively passive and disadvantaged position. Therefore, when handling business for customers, bank staff should strictly adhere to work processes and business operation standards, and fulfill the utmost duty of care and risk warning obligations.
keywords_en: Civil; Bank Card Dispute; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Liaoning Province; Natural Person; Financial Institution; Contract Law; Responsibility for Activating Online Banking; Obligation to Deliver U-Shield; Depositor's Duty of Care; Standard for Calculating Interest; Reversal of Judgment; Bank Card Account Opening; Online Banking Activation; Deposits Transferred Away; Forged Signature; Good Faith; Application for Retrial; Bank Card Dispute with Panjin Branch of a Limited Company
full_text_en:
Yi Lijun v. China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Panjin Branch — dispute over bank card

【Ruling Summary】

As a professional institution handling financial business, a bank holds an obvious, dominant, and advantageous position when handling services such as savings for natural persons, whereas natural persons are in a relatively passive and disadvantaged status. Therefore, when handling business for clients, bank employees should strictly follow work procedures and business operation standards, and exercise the utmost duty of care and risk warning obligations.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Supreme People's Court Min Zai No. 174

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Yi Lijun, male, Manchu ethnicity, born on March 30, 1959, residing in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hongwei, lawyer at Liaoning Zhiran Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Tingjiang, lawyer at Liaoning Qianjiang Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Panjin Branch. Address: No. 9, Shifu Street, Xinglongtai District, Panjin City, Liaoning Province.

Responsible Person: Guo Wenfeng, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wu Jie, lawyer at Beijing Longan Law Firm Shenyang Office.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zhigang, lawyer at Beijing Longan Law Firm Shenyang Office.

In the dispute over a bank card between the retrial applicant Yi Lijun and the respondent China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Panjin Branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Panjin Branch), Yi Lijun, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2016) Liao Min Zhong No. 502 of the High People's Court of Liaoning Province, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2017) Supreme People's Court Min Shen No. 555 dated April 14, 2017, decided to bring this case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing in this case. The retrial applicant Yi Lijun's agents ad litem Zhang Hongwei and Zheng Tingjiang, and the respondent ICBC Panjin Branch's agent ad litem Wang Zhigang appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Yi Lijun applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. Regarding the allocation of responsibility for the second activation of online banking on June 28, 2011. The second instance judgment held that Yi Lijun had signed and confirmed on the application form when activating online banking for the second time, and did not request the U-shield from the bank staff, resulting in the deposit being transferred out, and failed to exercise reasonable duty of care, thus ordering Yi Lijun to bear 40% of the secondary liability. This allocation of responsibility is clearly erroneous. The first instance court commissioned Liaoning Jiuzhou Judicial Expertise Institute to conduct a handwriting identification on Yi Lijun's signature on the online banking documents. The conclusion of the "Liaoning Jiuzhou Judicial Expertise Institute Document Examination Opinion" (hereinafter referred to as the "Expert Opinion") is that the signature on the activation application form was Yi Lijun's, but the signatures on the cancellation application for the first online banking and the handover confirmation form were not his own signature. In fact, Zhao Yuhong, a staff member of ICBC Panjin Branch, had asked Yi Lijun to sign multiple documents when opening the bank card, and Yi Lijun did not know that he was signing the online banking activation application. This is evident from the interrogation records of Yi Lijun and several other victims in the public security authorities; each victim depositor did not know that Zhao Yuhong had activated online banking for them. Moreover, if Yi Lijun had truly applied to activate online banking, there would have been no need for ICBC Panjin Branch to forge Yi Lijun's signature on the cancellation application for the first online banking and the handover confirmation form for receiving the U-shield; ICBC Panjin Branch could have simply asked Yi Lijun to sign those two documents. The above evidence can fully presume that Yi Lijun was unaware of the second activation of online banking. Furthermore, even if Yi Lijun knew about the activation of online banking, according to bank regulations, it should be the teller who hands over the U-shield to the depositor, not another person. Handing over the U-shield to the depositor is the bank's responsibility. The second instance judgment, on the ground that Yi Lijun did not request the U-shield from the staff, ordering him to bear 40% of the responsibility, is clearly improper. This case should hold ICBC Panjin Branch fully liable, and it should pay Yi Lijun the deposit of RMB 14,498,470. Even if Yi Lijun bears responsibility, a 40% share is excessively high and clearly unfair to Yi Lijun. 2. Regarding the interest standard. Yi Lijun argues that interest should be calculated according to the bank's loan interest rate for the same period. The second instance court held that since this case involves a demand deposit, interest should be calculated according to the demand deposit rate. Yi Lijun believes that since the public security authorities notified Yi Lijun in April 2012 that the money in his bank card had been transferred out and took away his bank card, Yi Lijun was unable to withdraw the deposit. Now, after the second instance found that ICBC Panjin Branch was at fault and ordered it to pay the deposit, ICBC Panjin Branch should pay interest to Yi Lijun at the loan interest rate from April 2012 onward. 3. Regarding whether Zhao Yuhong is suspected of committing a crime and whether the court should transfer the case materials to the public security authorities. From the interrogation records of Li Xuewu, Zhao Yuhong, and several victims submitted by Yi Lijun to the public security authorities, it can be seen that the deceived depositors did not know that Zhao Yuhong had unilaterally activated online banking for them, while Li Xuewu and Zhao Yuhong admitted that Li Xuewu had asked Zhao Yuhong to activate online banking for the victims and hand over the U-shields to Li Xuewu. Zhao Yuhong was clearly involved in joint criminal activity. The Expert Opinion further proves the above facts. Regarding whether Zhao Yuhong constitutes a crime, although the public security authorities and the procuratorate released her and withdrew the prosecution on grounds of insufficient evidence, the Expert Opinion is new evidence that emerged after the withdrawal of prosecution and is sufficient to affect the characterization of whether Zhao Yuhong's actions constitute a crime. Therefore, the court should submit the above leads and materials to the public security authorities. In summary, the second instance judgment has unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law. Yi Lijun requests the revocation of the first and second instance judgments, an order that ICBC Panjin Branch pay Yi Lijun the deposit of RMB 14,498,470 plus interest, and that the litigation costs be borne by ICBC Panjin Branch.

ICBC Panjin Branch argued in defense: 1. The second instance's determination of responsibility for activating online banking is correct. First, the signature at the "Applicant's Signature" on the June 28, 2011 electronic banking business application form was confirmed by judicial handwriting identification to be Yi Lijun's own handwriting. The application form clearly contains the notation "You have activated online banking and received the U-shield...". Yi Lijun's signature confirms that he had read this notice, but Yi Lijun did not request the U-shield from ICBC Panjin Branch staff. Second, Yi Lijun twice came to ICBC Panjin Branch to open accounts, both times in person with valid identification. Yi Lijun failed to exercise reasonable protection and duty of care with respect to his personal valid documents and information, which was also one of the reasons leading to the transfer of the deposit in question. Therefore, he should bear corresponding responsibility. Thus, the second instance's allocation of responsibility for the transfer of the deposit was correct. 2. ICBC Panjin Branch staff member Zhao Yuhong did not commit any criminal acts, and the case materials should not be transferred to the public security authorities. 3. ICBC Panjin Branch should not pay Yi Lijun loan interest. The legal relationship between the parties is a bank card deposit relationship, and Yi Lijun opened a demand deposit card. The deposit in question was withdrawn by Li Xuewu; ICBC Panjin Branch did not actually possess or use it. ICBC Panjin Branch is also a victim in the criminal case, and Li Xuewu has been held criminally liable. Therefore, Yi Lijun's claim that ICBC Panjin Branch should pay interest at the loan interest rate has no factual or legal basis. In summary, the second instance judgment has clear factual findings and correct application of law. ICBC Panjin Branch requests that Yi Lijun's retrial application be dismissed.

Yi Lijun filed a lawsuit with the Panjin Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) requesting: ICBC Panjin Branch to pay Yi Lijun deposit principal of RMB 14,500,000 plus interest (calculated from the date of deposit to the date of judgment payment, at the loan interest rate for the same period of the People's Bank of China for time deposits).

The court of first instance found the following facts: In April 2011, Yi Lijun was introduced to Li Xuewu through an acquaintance. Li Xuewu, together with criminal defendant Zhou Tong and others, fabricated false facts that the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China offered high interest to attract depositors and that the bank had investment projects requiring funds, using the lure of high interest to gain Yi Lijun's trust, and instructed Yi Lijun to open an account at the Liaohe Road Savings Office of ICBC Panjin Branch, Panshan Sub-branch. On April 26, 2011, at 15:44, Yi Lijun opened an account at the Liaohe Road Savings Office (account number 0714...2160, card number 6222...4354). Online banking was activated for this account at 15:50 on the same day (the depositor's signature for this online banking was not Yi Lijun's own handwriting, and ICBC Panjin Branch stated there was no U-shield receipt procedure). On the same day, Yi Lijun deposited RMB 4,000,000 into this account. On May 13, 2011, Yi Lijun deposited RMB 2,000,000 into this account, totaling RMB 6,000,000. From April 26, 2011, to May 14, 2011, RMB 5,999,010 was transferred out of this account via online banking, leaving a balance of RMB 601.07. On June 28, 2011, at 10:55, Yi Lijun again opened an account at the Liaohe Road Savings Office (account number 0714...9644, card number 6222...6284). Online banking was activated for this account at 11:07 on the same day, but Yi Lijun only signed the "ICBC Personal Client Business Application Form" for activating online banking and did not sign for receipt of the U-shield. (Before Yi Lijun opened this account, the previous online banking was cancelled; the signature on the cancellation procedure was also not Yi Lijun's own handwriting, and the words "card lost, cancel online banking" on that form were admitted by Zhao Yuhong, the teller responsible for handling Yi Lijun's account opening at ICBC Panjin Branch, as written by her.) From June 28, 2011, to November 11, 2011, Yi Lijun made nine deposits totaling RMB 8,500,000 into this account, and a total of RMB 8,499,460 was transferred out via online banking, leaving a balance of RMB 256.12. Yi Lijun opened two accounts at the same savings office, depositing a total of RMB 14,500,000. Both accounts opened on April 26, 2011, and June 28, 2011, were demand deposit accounts. Li Xuewu took a total of RMB 14,498,470 of Yi Lijun's deposits via online banking transfers or payments. Li Xuewu paid Yi Lijun a total of RMB 3,100,000 in "interest." When Yi Lijun opened the accounts at ICBC Panjin Branch, Li Xuewu was an employee of ICBC Panjin Branch, later having his labor relationship terminated by the branch. Yi Lijun and ICBC Panjin Branch have differing accounts of who handed over the U-shield to Li Xuewu upon activation of online banking. The court of first instance separately took statements from Yi Lijun and Zhao Yuhong. Zhao Yuhong stated: "There were cases where clients left their U-shields at the counter, and I gave them to Li Xuewu three or four times. Li Xuewu said that the client had agreed with him and left the U-shield, asking Li Xuewu to pick it up, so I gave it to him." The court of first instance asked Li Xuewu, who stated, "I asked Zhao Yuhong to activate Yi Lijun's online banking. After activation, Zhao Yuhong gave me the U-shield." The first and second instance courts found Li Xuewu guilty of fraud and sentenced him to 14 years' imprisonment. Li Xuewu's fraud crimes included the portion of Yi Lijun's deposits that were defrauded. However, the criminal judgment did not determine how the U-shield came into Zhao Yuhong's hands. At trial, Yi Lijun examined the signatures on the online banking procedures provided by ICBC Panjin Branch and stated that none of them were his own. Therefore, Yi Lijun applied for handwriting identification. The court of first instance commissioned Liaoning Jiuzhou Judicial Expertise Institute to conduct a handwriting identification on Yi Lijun's signatures on the online banking documents. The identification opinion confirmed: The signature "Yi Lijun" at the "Applicant's Signature" on the April 26, 2011 "ICBC Personal Client Business Application Form" (for activating online banking), the signature "Yi Lijun" at the "Signature" on the June 28, 2011 "ICBC Electronic Banking Personal Client Change (Cancellation) Item Application Form," and the signature "Yi Lijun" at the "Receiver 1 Seal" on the June 28, 2011 "ICBC Handover Confirmation Form" (for U-shield handover) were not Yi Lijun's handwriting; the signature "Yi Lijun" at the "Applicant's Signature" on the June 26, 2011 "ICBC Personal Client Business Application Form" (for activating online banking) was Yi Lijun's handwriting.

The court of first instance ruled: 1. ICBC Panjin Branch shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Yi Lijun 60% of the deposit of RMB 11,398,470 (RMB 14,498,470 - RMB 3,100,000), i.e., RMB 6,839,082, and pay interest on the above deposit at the demand deposit interest rate of the same period of ICBC (interest on RMB 4,000,000 from April 26, 2011; on RMB 1,999,010 from May 13, 2011; on RMB 840,072 from November 11, 2011; up to the date of payment as determined). If ICBC Panjin Branch fails to perform the monetary payment obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall double the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. 2. Dismiss Yi Lijun's other claims.

ICBC Panjin Branch, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the High People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance) requesting: 1. Revoke the first instance judgment and dismiss Yi Lijun's claims; 2. Yi Lijun to bear the litigation costs. Yi Lijun, also dissatisfied, appealed to the court of second instance requesting: 1. Revoke the first instance judgment and amend it; 2. Order ICBC Panjin Branch to pay Yi Lijun the deposit of RMB 14,498,470 plus interest; 3. Litigation costs to be borne by ICBC Panjin Branch.

The court of second instance confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance. The court of second instance additionally found that Li Xuewu was originally an employee of ICBC Panjin Branch, and on July 20, 2011, his labor contract was terminated by the branch. On December 19, 2014, Panshan County People's Court of Liaoning Province found Li Xuewu guilty of fraud and sentenced him to 14 years' imprisonment, with confiscation of all personal property. Li Xuewu appealed, and the Panjin Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province upheld the first instance judgment. The criminal judgments from both instances found: During the period from May 2010 to March 2012, at the suggestion of defendant Li Xuewu, he and co-defendant Zhou Tong, using the lure of high interest, or fabricating false facts that the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China offered high interest to attract depositors and that the bank had investment projects requiring funds, or falsely representing Li Xuewu as an employee of ICBC Panjin Branch or Panshan Sub-branch, directly or through intermediaries, gained the trust of victims, instructed victims to deposit funds into ICBC Panjin Panlong Sub-branch and Liaohe Road Savings Office, and then defendant Li Xuewu took the victims' deposits by online banking transfers, bank counter transfers, cash withdrawals, or online payments, and dissipated the stolen proceeds with defendant Zhou Tong. ... In April 2011, defendant Li Xuewu gained the trust of victim Yi Lijun, instructed Yi Lijun to open an account at Liaohe Road Savings Office, and Yi Lijun deposited a total of RMB 14,500,000 between April 26 and November 11, 2011. Li Xuewu took RMB 14,498,470 of Yi Lijun's deposits by online banking transfers or payments. It was also found that after Yi Lijun opened an account at Liaohe Road Savings Office, a subordinate of ICBC Panjin Branch, on June 28, 2011, Yi Lijun made nine deposits totaling RMB 8,500,000 into that account from the account opening date to November 11, 2011, respectively: RMB 1,000,000 on the account opening day, RMB 2,000,000 on June 29, RMB 1,000,000 on July 6, RMB 1,500,000 on July 27, RMB 500,000 on August 8, RMB 2,000,000 on August 26, and RMB 500,000 on November 11.

The court of second instance found as follows: 1. Regarding whether the legal nature of the relationship in dispute was a personal loan relationship between Li Xuewu and Yi Lijun, or a savings deposit contract relationship between ICBC Panjin Branch and Yi Lijun. According to the criminal judgments of Panshan County People's Court and Panjin Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province, Yi Lijun deposited funds with ICBC Panjin Branch for the purpose of obtaining high interest from the bank, and had no intention to lend funds to Li Xuewu personally. Although Li Xuewu took away Yi Lijun's deposits, he also induced Yi Lijun to deposit funds with the bank by fabricating high interest returns from ICBC; that is, it was the bank, not Li Xuewu personally, that accepted the deposits. Therefore, there was no mutual agreement to establish a loan relationship between the parties. Based on the facts that Yi Lijun applied to ICBC Panjin Branch to open a current savings account, ICBC Panjin Branch opened the account and issued a bank debit card, and Yi Lijun deposited funds into that bank card, it can be determined that the legal relationship in dispute was a savings deposit contract relationship between ICBC Panjin Branch and Yi Lijun. 2. Regarding whether the appraisal procedure in the "Expert Conclusion Report" was illegal and whether the appraisal conclusion should be admitted. ICBC Panjin Branch argued that the extraction of the test materials in the "Expert Conclusion Report" violated the relevant provisions of Article 24, Paragraph 4 of the "General Rules on Judicial Appraisal Procedures". Some samples were signed by only one person who retrieved them, without an on-site witness; some samples were signed by only two persons present, without the signature of the person who extracted the samples. Therefore, the branch argued that the appraisal conclusion made by the appraisal authority based on invalid appraisal samples should not be admitted. Upon review, the pages to which ICBC Panjin Branch raised objections contained signatures from Part 5 "Samples" of the "Expert Conclusion Report". That is, these pages only pertained to appraisal "samples", not the "test materials" referred to in the "General Rules on Judicial Appraisal Procedures". The provisions of Article 24, Paragraph 4 of the "General Rules on Judicial Appraisal Procedures" do not apply to these "samples". Therefore, there was no procedural illegality in the appraisal conclusion in dispute, and it should be admitted. 3. Regarding whether the staff of ICBC Panjin Branch engaged in irregular operations in handling the online banking business. According to the relevant provisions of the "Administrative Measures for Electronic Banking Business of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China", when handling online banking business, tellers must carefully verify the customer's identity and the contents of the application form. Applying to open online banking must be done by the applicant in person. The U-shield or electronic banking password card must be delivered to the customer in person. Relevant documents for handling online banking business must be signed by the customer in person. Based on the "Expert Conclusion Report", the court of second instance found that the online banking opened for "Yi Lijun" by ICBC Panjin Branch on April 26, 2011 was not handled by Yi Lijun himself. When ICBC Panjin Branch cancelled this online banking business on June 28, 2011, it was also not upon Yi Lijun's own application. Although ICBC Panjin Branch opened online banking upon Yi Lijun's application on June 28, 2011, it did not deliver the U-shield to Yi Lijun personally. Therefore, ICBC Panjin Branch engaged in irregular operations in both handling the opening and cancellation of Yi Lijun's online banking business. 4. Regarding whether Yi Lijun fulfilled his duty of care in the account opening process and whether he was at fault for the transfer of the deposits. The deposits of Yi Lijun involved in this case were all taken away by Li Xuewu through online banking transfers or payments. Therefore, the opening of online banking, the control of the U-shield, and the acquisition of the online banking password were the key factors in the fraud of the funds in dispute. According to the evidence in the case, after opening the account on April 26, 2011, Yi Lijun did not open online banking, so there was no issue of his handing over the U-shield to others or leaking the online banking password. Although he obtained corresponding high interest, there was no direct causal relationship between his being lured by high interest to deposit funds and the loss of funds. Therefore, Yi Lijun had no fault whatsoever for the loss of funds in the bank card opened on April 26, 2011. However, when Yi Lijun opened the account on June 28, 2011, he also signed an application form to confirm the opening of online banking services. This application form contained a prompt in large font: "You have activated online banking and received a U-shield. With the U-shield, you can conduct online transfers, remittances, and other services. Please keep the U-shield properly, do not give it to others, and remember the online banking and U-shield passwords. Do not disclose them." However, Yi Lijun did not pay attention to the contents of this prompt, nor did he proactively request the online banking U-shield from the staff of ICBC Panjin Branch. Instead, after opening the account and online banking, he transferred a huge amount of funds into this account, which allowed criminals to use the U-shield to transfer the deposits in his card, causing the loss in dispute. In handling this account opening and deposit business, he failed to exercise a reasonable and prudent duty of care commensurate with the business from which he expected to obtain benefits. Therefore, he was somewhat at fault for the transfer of the funds deposited after opening the account on June 28, 2011. 5. Regarding whether the high interest of RMB 3.1 million received by Yi Lijun should be deducted. The account Yi Lijun opened with ICBC Panjin Branch was a current savings deposit account. The current interest on the funds deposited by Yi Lijun was not this amount. According to the criminal judgment, this RMB 3.1 million was paid by Li Xuewu. Li Xuewu paid this amount to Yi Lijun as high interest to deceive Yi Lijun into losing control of his account in order to defraud the bank deposits. Therefore, it should be deducted when returning the principal of the deposit. Yi Lijun argued that the RMB 3.1 million paid by Li Xuewu involved a different legal relationship from this case and should not be deducted from the payment. However, since there was no loan relationship between Yi Lijun and Li Xuewu, there was no reason for Li Xuewu to make such a payment, so this argument was clearly untenable. 6. Regarding whether the relevant materials should be transferred to the public security authority on the grounds that Zhao Yuhong was suspected of committing a crime. According to the "Expert Conclusion Report", the signatures on the applications for opening and canceling online banking on April 26 and June 28, 2011, were not Yi Lijun's own signatures. However, this "Expert Conclusion Report" did not confirm that the signatures were made by Zhao Yuhong. Even if they were made by Zhao Yuhong, if it could not be determined that Zhao Yuhong acted with subjective intent, such conduct would merely be a violation of operational procedures and internal bank management regulations. In this regard, both the public security authority and the procuratorate had previously detained Zhao Yuhong criminally or initiated public prosecutions on charges of embezzlement or fraud, but later released him or withdrew the prosecutions due to insufficient evidence. Therefore, transferring the materials in dispute to the public security authority on the grounds that Zhao Yuhong was suspected of committing a crime lacked sufficient basis. In summary, the court of first instance found that ICBC Panjin Branch should bear primary liability because its staff violated banking operational procedures by handing over the customer's U-shield to others, resulting in deposit losses. Yi Lijun should bear secondary liability for failing to exercise reasonable care. The determination of the respective liability ratios was not improper. However, the decision that Yi Lijun should bear 40% of the liability for the losses arising from the online banking opened on April 26, 2011 lacked sufficient basis and should be corrected.

The court of second instance ruled as follows: 1. Item 2 of the main text of the civil judgment of first instance was vacated. 2. Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment of first instance was amended to: ICBC Panjin Branch shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Yi Lijun RMB 9,238,686 in deposits, plus interest on the said deposits at the current deposit interest rate of ICBC for the same period from the respective deposit dates until the date of payment determined in this judgment (interest on RMB 4 million from April 26, 2011; interest on RMB 1,999,010 from May 13, 2011; interest on RMB 3,239,676 [(8,499,460 - 3,100,000) x 60%] from November 11, 2011). 3. Yi Lijun's other claims were dismissed. If ICBC Panjin Branch fails to perform the monetary obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 108,800 shall be borne by ICBC Panjin Branch in the amount of RMB 69,310 and by Yi Lijun in the amount of RMB 39,490. The bearing of the appraisal fees shall be executed according to the first instance judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 108,800 shall be borne by ICBC Panjin Branch in the amount of RMB 75,554 and by Yi Lijun in the amount of RMB 33,246.

This Court confirms the facts found by the courts of first and second instance.

Upon retrial, this Court finds that, based on the judgments of first and second instance, Yi Lijun's retrial requests, and ICBC Panjin Branch's defense submissions, the main issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether a savings deposit contract relationship existed between ICBC Panjin Branch and Yi Lijun; 2. How liability for the transfer of the deposits in dispute should be apportioned; 3. Whether the high interest of RMB 3.1 million received by Yi Lijun should be deducted and the method for calculating interest on the deposits in dispute.

Regarding whether a savings deposit contract relationship existed between ICBC Panjin Branch and Yi Lijun. Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A civil juristic act shall meet the following conditions: (1) the actor has the corresponding capacity for civil conduct; (2) the expression of intent is genuine; (3) it does not violate the law or public interests." In this case, the criminal judgment of Panjin Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province [(2015) Pan Zhong Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 00013] found: "Between May 2010 and March 2012, Li Xuewu, in collusion with others, induced victims by offering high interest or by fabricating false facts that ICBC offered high interest to attract deposits or that ICBC had investment projects requiring funds, or by fabricating Li Xuewu's identity as a staff member of ICBC Panjin Branch or Panshan Sub-branch. He contacted victims directly or through intermediaries, deceived them, and instructed them to deposit funds with Panlong Sub-branch and Liaohe Road Savings Office of ICBC Panjin Branch. The defendant Li Xuewu then took away the victims' deposits by online banking transfers, bank counter transfers, cash withdrawals, or online payments. ... In April 2011, the defendant Li Xuewu deceived the victim Yi Lijun, instructed Yi Lijun to open an account at Liaohe Road Savings Office, and deposited a total of RMB 14.5 million between April 26, 2011 and November 11, 2011." Based on this, this Court finds that Yi Lijun's genuine expression of intent was to deposit funds with the bank to obtain high interest. The savings deposit contract relationship between Yi Lijun and the bank was established from the time the bank accepted Yi Lijun's deposits and delivered the deposit vouchers. Although Yi Lijun deposited the funds in dispute under the inducement of Li Xuewu's fabrication of high interest returns, this circumstance does not affect the legality and validity of the savings deposit contract between Yi Lijun and ICBC Panjin Branch. In this case, Yi Lijun applied to open current savings deposit accounts at Liaohe Road Savings Office, a subordinate of ICBC Panjin Branch, on April 26 and June 28, 2011. Accordingly, the branch delivered two bank debit cards to Yi Lijun. Between April 26, 2011 and November 11, 2011, Yi Lijun deposited a total of RMB 14.5 million into these two accounts. The above facts are sufficient to prove that a savings deposit contract relationship had been established between Yi Lijun and ICBC Panjin Branch. The bank debit card issued by ICBC Panjin Branch to Yi Lijun is direct evidence of the establishment of the savings deposit contract relationship between the parties. Based on the facts that Yi Lijun applied to ICBC Panjin Branch to open current savings accounts, ICBC Panjin Branch opened the accounts and issued bank debit cards, and Yi Lijun deposited funds into these bank cards, this Court finds that the savings deposit contract relationship between ICBC Panjin Branch and Yi Lijun was established.

Regarding how liability for the transfer of the deposits in dispute should be apportioned. In this case, Yi Lijun's deposits were all illegally taken by Li Xuewu through online banking transfers or payments. The opening of online banking, the control of the U-shield, and the acquisition of the online banking password were the key factors in the fraud of the funds in dispute. Clarifying whether ICBC Panjin Branch engaged in irregular operations in handling the online banking business for Yi Lijun and whether Yi Lijun fulfilled his duty of care in the process of opening online banking is the prerequisite for apportioning liability for the losses in dispute.

(1) Regarding whether ICBC Panjin Branch engaged in irregular operations in handling the online banking business for Yi Lijun. Article 1, Section 2, Chapter 7 "Personal Online Banking Business" of the "Administrative Measures for Electronic Banking Business of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China" provides: "The teller shall carefully review the contents of the application form and verify the customer's identity before handling online banking registration for the customer. ... The teller shall, in accordance with the principle of 'handled by the person, delivered to the person, signed by the person', deliver the U-shield or electronic banking password card to the customer applying for online banking in person. The on-site authorized person or on-site management personnel shall supervise the delivery of the U-shield to the customer in person and confirm that the customer has signed for receipt in person." Accordingly, when handling online banking business, tellers must carefully verify the customer's identity and the contents of the application form. Applying to open online banking must be done by the applicant in person. The U-shield or electronic banking password card must be delivered to the customer in person. Relevant documents for handling online banking business must be signed by the customer in person. However, the "Expert Conclusion Report" confirmed that the "Yi Lijun" signature at the "Applicant Signature" on the "ICBC Personal Customer Business Application Form" (Electronic Banking Registration / Bank Account Service Opening) dated April 26, 2011, the "Yi Lijun" signature at the "Signature" on the "ICBC Electronic Banking Personal Customer Change (Cancellation) Matters Application Form" dated June 28, 2011, and the "Yi Lijun" signature at the "Receiver 1 Stamp" on the "ICBC Handover Confirmation (U-shield Handover)" dated June 28, 2011, were all not Yi Lijun's signatures. Obviously, the online banking opened for "Yi Lijun" by ICBC Panjin Branch on April 26, 2011 was not handled by Yi Lijun himself. When ICBC Panjin Branch cancelled this online banking business on June 28, 2011, it was also not upon Yi Lijun's own application. Although ICBC Panjin Branch opened online banking upon Yi Lijun's application on June 28, 2011, it did not deliver the U-shield to Yi Lijun personally. Therefore, ICBC Panjin Branch engaged in serious irregular operations in both handling the opening and cancellation of Yi Lijun's online banking business on April 26, 2011 and June 28, 2011.

(2) Whether Yi Lijun fulfilled his duty of care in the process of opening online banking. In this case, after opening the account on April 26, 2011, Yi Lijun did not open online banking, so there was no issue of his handing over the U-shield to others or leaking the online banking password. Although he obtained corresponding high interest, there was no direct causal relationship between his being lured by high interest to deposit funds and the loss of funds. Therefore, it is difficult to find that Yi Lijun was at fault for the loss of funds in the bank card opened on April 26, 2011. However, when Yi Lijun opened the account on June 28, 2011, he also signed an application form to confirm the activation of online banking services. This application form contained a prompt in large font: "You have activated online banking and received a U-shield. With the U-shield, you can conduct online transfers, remittances, and other services. Please keep the U-shield properly, do not give it to others, and remember the online banking and U-shield passwords. Do not disclose them." However, Yi Lijun did not pay attention to the contents of this application form, nor did he proactively request the online banking U-shield from the staff of ICBC Panjin Branch. Instead, after opening the account and online banking, he transferred a huge amount of funds into this account, which allowed criminals to use the U-shield to transfer the deposits in his card, causing the loss of deposits in dispute. In handling this account opening and deposit business, he failed to exercise a reasonable and prudent duty of care commensurate with the business from which he expected to obtain benefits. Therefore, he was somewhat negligent for the transfer of the funds deposited after opening the account on June 28, 2011.

3. Regarding the Liability for the Transfer of the Deposit Funds Involved in the Case. First, Article 6 of the Commercial Banking Law of the PRC stipulates: "Commercial banks shall protect the lawful rights and interests of depositors from infringement by any entity or individual." Banks have a statutory duty to ensure the safety of depositors' deposits. In the context of the information, electronic, and technological era, society has developed rapidly, the division of labor has become increasingly refined, social relations have become more complex, and the public's reliance on specialization has grown ever greater. Modern commercial banks, as enterprise legal persons and specialized financial institutions that engage in businesses such as absorbing public deposits, granting loans, and handling settlements, not only have traditional economic functions but also bear a large number of social functions. By leveraging technology, they have developed many new businesses, enhancing their own competitiveness while serving society and customers, and enjoy a very high degree of trust and credibility among the general public, thereby enjoying a high reputation. When ordinary depositors go to banks to handle savings business, the business environment, standardized services, and technological means, on the one hand, give ordinary customers who lack financial knowledge a sense of security, and the corresponding duty of care is correspondingly reduced. On the other hand, under the circumstances of cumbersome procedures, a large number of specialized terms, complex technological services, and the possibility that many other customers are waiting behind them, it is objectively difficult for ordinary customers to exercise the utmost duty of care even if they wish to do so. More often than not, they can only passively follow the arrangements of bank staff and handle business according to the procedures instructed by bank staff. More obligations mean greater responsibility. Banks should fulfill a greater duty of care and bear a strict duty to ensure the safety of depositors' deposits. They should formulate sound business rules and strengthen internal management. During the process of handling business between the bank and ordinary depositors, the bank's staff, representing the bank, should more strictly abide by work procedures and operational norms. In this case, the facts that on April 26, 2011, the online banking service for Yi Lijun was opened without his application, and that on June 28, 2011, the staff of ICBC Panjin Branch violated operational rules by handling the U-Shield business without authorization and handing the U-Shield to another person, directly led to the loss of the deposit funds involved in the case. ICBC Panjin Branch should bear the primary and overwhelming majority of the liability for the loss of the deposit funds involved in the case. Second, during his employment at ICBC Panjin Branch, Li Xuewu used his work identity to fabricate the lie of high-interest deposit solicitation, inducing Yi Lijun to deposit the funds involved in the case into ICBC Panjin Branch, and exploited his work convenience to take the U-Shield from his colleague Zhao Yuhong, resulting in the loss of the funds involved. The above facts prove that ICBC Panjin Branch had loopholes in its internal management and that its staff seriously violated operational rules. ICBC Panjin Branch should bear the liability for inadequate management for the losses involved in the case. In the context where bank staff participating in financial fraud crimes occur from time to time, banks should further prevent such incidents, strengthen internal management, and provide customers with more high-quality, safe, and reassuring services. Third, Yi Lijun, as a natural person with full capacity for civil conduct, was tempted by the high-interest deposit solicitation of ICBC Panjin Branch staff Li Xuewu, believed the lies of the criminal Li Xuewu, went to the counter of ICBC Panjin Branch to open an account, open a card, and activate online banking services, and deposited a total of RMB 14.5 million in large amounts into the account. In the context where criminals use the internet for fraud, bank card-related fraud cases occur frequently, and public security organs widely publicize in bank premises and other public places to prevent criminals from using bank cards for fraud, Yi Lijun, as a natural person with full capacity for civil conduct, should have exercised the utmost duty of care when enjoying high returns and depositing large amounts of funds. However, he not only failed to exercise the utmost duty of care but also lowered his risk prevention awareness and relaxed his duty of care for the safety of funds in the account. This led to his failure to carefully read the prompts on the application form for activating online banking when opening the account and activating online banking services on June 28, 2011, and failure to proactively request the U-Shield from the bank. As a result, the criminal used the U-Shield to transfer the deposits from his card, causing the loss of the deposit funds involved. In handling this account opening and deposit business, he failed to exercise the corresponding, reasonable, and prudent duty of care and should bear a secondary and minor liability for the transfer of the total of RMB 8.5 million deposited into the account in nine installments from the date of account opening on June 28, 2011, to November 11, 2011.

In summary, this court holds that banks, as specialized institutions handling financial business, occupy an obvious, dominant, and advantageous position when handling savings and other businesses for natural persons, while natural persons are in a relatively passive and disadvantaged position. Therefore, when bank staff handle business for customers, they should strictly abide by work procedures and business operation norms and fulfill the utmost duty of care and risk reminder obligations. In this case, Yi Lijun did not activate online banking services on April 26, 2011, and should not bear liability for the losses caused by the online banking opened on that date. However, for the online banking activated on June 28, 2011, Yi Lijun failed to exercise the corresponding, reasonable, and prudent duty of care that he should have exercised in line with the expected benefits of the business. He should bear 1% of the liability for the transfer of most of the funds from that deposit by the criminal through online banking. ICBC Panjin Branch, under its strict duty to ensure the safety of depositors' deposits, failed to exercise strict internal management, resulting in loopholes in internal management and serious violation of operational rules by its staff, and failed to fulfill the utmost duty of care and risk reminder obligations. It should bear 99% of the liability. The determination of liability for the loss from this deposit by the court of second instance was improper, and this court corrects it.

Regarding the issue of whether the RMB 3.1 million in high interest received by Yi Lijun should be deducted and the method for calculating interest on the deposits involved in the case. In this case, there was no loan relationship between Yi Lijun and Li Xuewu. The RMB 3.1 million that Yi Lijun received from Li Xuewu had no legal basis and was high interest paid by Li Xuewu to gain Yi Lijun's trust and thereby obtain control of the online banking U-Shield to control the account. Therefore, this amount should be deducted when ICBC Panjin Branch returns the deposit principal. As for Yi Lijun's claim that interest on the deposits involved should be calculated at the bank's loan interest rate for the corresponding period, since Yi Lijun conducted demand deposit business, this claim lacks factual and legal basis, and this court does not support it.

In conclusion, Yi Lijun's retrial requests are partially established. Pursuant to Article 207, Paragraph 1 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2014) Pan Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00035 of the Panjin Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province;

2. Set aside the civil judgment (2016) Liao Min Zhong No. 502 of the Liaoning High People's Court;

3. The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Panjin Branch shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay Yi Lijun RMB 11,344,475, and shall pay interest on the said deposits at the contemporaneous demand deposit interest rate of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China from the respective deposit dates to the date of payment determined by this judgment (interest shall be calculated on RMB 4 million from April 26, 2011; on RMB 1,999,010 from May 13, 2011; and on RMB 5,345,465 [(8,499,460 - 3,100,000) x 99%] from November 11, 2011);

4. Dismiss Yi Lijun's other claims.

If the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Panjin Branch fails to perform the pecuniary obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall, pursuant to Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 108,800, to be borne by the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Panjin Branch in the amount of RMB 107,712 and by Yi Lijun in the amount of RMB 1,088. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 168,474, to be borne by the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Panjin Branch in the amount of RMB 166,789 and by Yi Lijun in the amount of RMB 1,685.
